newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Fust increases stake in Jelmoli.
newsitem.headline: Fust increases stake in Jelmoli.

text.p: Investor Walter Fust has acquired a majority stake in Swiss retail group Jelmoli AG, increasing his share in its capital to 51.9 percent from 11.3 percent, Fust said in a press statement.
At the same time, Fust declared that Jelmoli would remain together as a group.

The Jelmoli concern, which has considerably pared down its holdings, now has a Zurich department store and properties, travel firm Imholz Reisen, and a stake in Dipl Ing Fust AG, a consumer electronics and appliance group.

Walter Fust sold the majority of Fust, the firm he founded, to Jelmoli two years ago, and has since seen the firm bearing his name dragged down by financial problems partly pertaining to the majority holders of Jelmoli, UTC.
Jelmoli's interests also include drycleaning chain Terlinden and opticians Kochoptik.

"The Jelmoli Holding AG owns an interesting portfolio of companies with strong earnings and good growth potential. It (Jelmoli) will therefore remain together in its current form, and will be developed further. There are no sales planned for any of its single firms," Fust said.
Fust's increased holding in Jelmoli reflected purchase of a package of 40.6 percent formerly held by UTC, a Basle-based private company representing roughly 200 shareholders.
UTC, which acquired Jelmoli in 1977, has been under pressure from creditor banks to reduce its debts.

The acquisition by Fust is an interim step in a complicated series of transactions which foresee leaving Fust with 28.6 percent of Jelmoli's capital, and giving Jelmoli a 100-percent stake in Dipl. Ing. Fust AG, the company set up by Fust.
The public, according to the plan, will ulimately own 62.8 percent of Jelmoli's capital, as opposed to 46.4 percent currently.
But Fust will retain the majority of voting of rights in Jelmoli under the plan.
The next transaction calls for Fust to exchange one share of Jelmoli for two shares of Dipl. Ing. Fust AG which will increase public shareholders' stake in Jelmoli
Meanwhile, the restructuring of Jelmoli was continuing according to plan, Fust added.
Jelmoli's sales fell 2.8 percent in the first half of 1996, but the company has said it expected better results for the year as a whole. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
